mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the past three months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past three months signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% YoY, the combined effect of high interest rates and inflationary pressures typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the interaction effect of high FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increases on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5 percentage points and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in the same month, the combined signal of a tightening labor market typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction effect of UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the past two months signals increased consumer confidence and demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of economic expansion, a sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the past six months signals strong economic fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between GDP increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during expansionary periods.
